}; let (id, amount) = (payment.id, payment.amount); let debit = scope.message(&Debit { id, amount }).publish().await; let credit = scope.message(&Credit { id, amount }).publish().await; if debit.is_err() || credit.is_err() { if let Err(err) = scope.abort().await { tracing::warn!(payment.id, %err, "payments: aborting the ledger transaction failed"); } return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } scope.commit().await.map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } } Macros Manual examples/transactional_publisher.rs fn app(broker: MemoryBroker) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ledger", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { // One transaction per batch, committed before the batch is acked. b.include(confirm.batch(nonzero!(64))) .out_reply(TransactionalPublish) .transactional() .include(book) .out(Ledger, TransactionalPublish) }) } examples/manual/transactional_publisher.rs fn app(broker: MemoryBroker) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ledger", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { // One transaction per batch, committed before the batch is acked. b.include( subscriber("orders", Confirm) .reply() .batch(nonzero!(64)) .build(), ) .out_reply(TransactionalPublish) .transactional() .include(subscriber("payments", Book).build()) .out(Ledger, TransactionalPublish) }) }

A handler answers a message by returning a value; the reply type or the mount site says where the answer goes. Every reply type derives Outgoing. A type with #[outgoing(name = "..")] fixes its destination, and the handler carries the bare clause #[subscriber("src", reply)]. A type that names nothing takes the destination from the clause, reply("dest"). A destination declared on the type wins over a name at the mount site, and startup logs a warning for such a registration. The forms of a destination are on the Destinations page. Result<Reply, HandlerOutcome> keeps the settlement in the handler's hands: Ok publishes the reply and acks, Err publishes nothing and settles by the outcome. A reply whose publish fails nacks the delivery with requeue, so a replying handler has to be safe to run twice. A batch handler returns one Vec of replies per batch. With nothing else said, the reply leaves through the broker's default policy under the default codec. .out_reply(policy) names the publish policy, and the steps after it complete the reply's wiring. .codec(..) names the codec of the reply, while the request still decodes with the scope's codec. .transform(..) adds a publish transform, and .transactional() puts every reply of a batch in one broker transaction. A broker that only reads the payload is lent the dispatch loop's own encode buffer, so a reply allocates nothing per delivery.

The reply type fixes its destination. Macros Manual examples/replies.rs /// The reply type fixes its destination, so the clause is the bare `reply`. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "receipts")] struct Receipt { order_id: u64, } /// `Ok` publishes the receipt and acks; `Err` publishes nothing and settles by the outcome. #[subscriber("orders", reply)] async fn issue_receipt(order: &Order) -> Result<Receipt, HandlerOutcome> { if order.id == 0 { return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); } Ok(Receipt { order_id: order.id }) } examples/manual/replies.rs /// The reply type fixes its destination, so the chain names none. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, schemars::JsonSchema)] struct Receipt { order_id: u64, } // `#[outgoing(name = "receipts")]` by hand. impl OutgoingDestination for Receipt { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "receipts"; } impl MessageHeaders for Receipt { type Contract = NoHeaders; } /// `Ok` publishes the receipt and acks; `Err` publishes nothing and settles by the outcome. struct IssueReceipt; impl Handle<Order, Receipt> for IssueReceipt { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Receipt, HandlerOutcome>> { if order.id == 0 { return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::drop())); } ready(Ok(Receipt { order_id: order.id })) } } The clause names the destination of a type that declares none. Macros Manual examples/replies.rs /// The reply type declares no destination, so the clause names one. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] struct Quote { order_id: u64, price: u64, } #[subscriber("quote-requests", reply("quotes"))] async fn quote(order: &Order) -> Quote { Quote { order_id: order.id, price: order.id * 10, } } examples/manual/replies.rs /// The reply type declares no destination, so the chain names one. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, schemars::JsonSchema)] struct Quote { order_id: u64, price: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Quote { type Form = CallerName; } impl MessageHeaders for Quote { type Contract = NoHeaders; } struct QuoteOrder; impl Handle<Order, Quote> for QuoteOrder { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Quote, HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(Quote { order_id: order.id, price: order.id * 10, })) } } Macros Manual examples/replies.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // The broker's default policy, under the default codec. b.include(issue_receipt) // The policy the reply leaves through, named at the mount site. .include(quote) .out_reply(Publish) }) } examples/manual/replies.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // The broker's default policy, under the default codec. b.include(subscriber("orders", IssueReceipt).reply().build()) // The destination the type leaves open, and the policy the reply leaves through. .include( subscriber("quote-requests", QuoteOrder) .reply() .to("quotes") .build(), ) .out_reply(Publish) }) }

A publish transform changes an outgoing message at one publish position, before it reaches the publisher. A transform belongs to one position: a reply, one slot, or the replies of a batch. It is static, so the chain of transforms is one type and costs only its own code. What it reads, which settings it writes and whether it names the destination are part of its type, so a transform mounted where it does not fit does not compile. The app-wide counterpart, which wraps every publish of the app, is the publish layer.

A batch publish transform is a step on the replies of a batch handler: each reply passes it on its own, with the batch's context. A batch handler with a reply returns one Vec of replies per batch, and those replies pass their own steps. .batch_transform(..) adds one after .out_reply(policy), and a single-message mount rejects it at compile time. The per-message publish transforms do not run on batch replies, and batch transforms do not run on single replies. for_batch lifts a per-message transform onto the batch path, so one impl serves both. All replies of a batch see one PublishContext, the batch's: its name is the subscription, its headers are empty, and its context fields are the broker's batch context. A transform that reads the message it answers belongs on a single-message handler. A batch reply never offers the naming right. A batch transform has no macro form: the same impl serves both forms, and only the mounting differs.

examples/batch_transform.rs /// Marks every reply of a batch. It sees the batch's context, not one delivery's. struct Batched; impl<C, Options> BatchPublishTransform<C, Options> for Batched { fn apply( &self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, _cx: &PublishContext<'_, C>, ) { out.headers_mut().insert("batched", "true"); } } /// A per-message transform, reused on the batch path through `for_batch`. struct Service(&'static str); impl<K: ContextKind, Options> PublishTransform<K, Options> for Service { type Destination = Reads; fn apply(&self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, _cx: &K::View<'_>) { out.headers_mut().insert("service", self.0); } } Macros Manual examples/batch_transform.rs fn app(broker: MemoryBroker) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(confirm.batch(nonzero!(64))) .out_reply(Publish) .batch_transform(Batched) .batch_transform(for_batch(Service("billing"))) }) } examples/manual/batch_transform.rs fn app(broker: MemoryBroker) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include( subscriber("orders", Confirm) .reply() .to("receipts") .batch(nonzero!(64)) .build(), ) .out_reply(Publish) .batch_transform(Batched) .batch_transform(for_batch(Service("billing"))) }) }

A naming transform sets the destination of each message, on a position where nothing else declared it: a reply to the inbox a request named. A transform that declares type Destination = Names may call set_name on the outgoing message. A position offers that right only where nothing declared the destination: a reply type with no #[outgoing(name = ..)], or a slot whose whole #[publishes(..)] list leaves it open. It offers it once, so a second naming transform on one position does not compile, and neither does one on a declared reply or on a batch reply. DefaultSlot and a slot that lists a declared destination never offer it. The name at the mount site stays the declared fallback: the generated document reports it, and a delivery the transform leaves alone is answered there. A name read off the delivery costs no copy: get_shared hands over the header's own buffer, and Str checks it is UTF-8. The reply side of RequestReply is the usual case. A naming transform is a publish transform in every other way: it has no macro form, and only the mounting differs.

examples/naming_transform.rs /// Answers on the inbox the question named in its `reply-to` header. The header's bytes become /// the destination as they are: one UTF-8 check, no copy. struct ToInbox; impl<C, Options> PublishTransform<ForReply<C>, Options> for ToInbox { type Destination = Names; fn apply( &self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, cx: &PublishContext<'_, C>, ) { if let Some(inbox) = cx.headers().get_shared("reply-to") && let Ok(name) = Str::try_from(inbox) { out.set_name(name); } } } Macros Manual examples/naming_transform.rs /// `"answers"` is the fallback, and what the generated document reports. #[subscriber("questions", reply("answers"))] async fn answer(question: &Question) -> Answer { Answer { id: question.id } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("answers", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { b.include(answer).out_reply(Publish).transform(ToInbox) }) } examples/manual/naming_transform.rs struct AnswerQuestion; impl Handle<Question, Answer> for AnswerQuestion { fn handle( &self, question: &Question, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Answer, HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(Answer { id: question.id })) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("answers", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // `"answers"` is the fallback, and what the generated document reports. b.include( subscriber("questions", AnswerQuestion) .reply() .to("answers") .build(), ) .out_reply(Publish) .transform(ToInbox) }) }

A publish transform is a static step on one publish position: it reads the delivery or the slot, and changes the outgoing message. .transform(..) adds one after the position it belongs to: after .out_reply(policy) for a reply, after .out(marker, policy) for a slot. Its apply gets the outgoing message, the broker's per-message settings and a view of the position, and returns nothing: it cannot refuse a publish. An impl declares three things. The kind is what it reads. ForReply<C> reads the delivery being answered through a PublishContext: its channel, headers and the broker's context fields. ForSlot reads a SlotContext, the slot's name and nothing else, because the body that publishes has already read its delivery. The Options parameter is the settings it writes: (), or the broker's own type, which mounts it only over that broker's publisher. type Destination is what it may do to the destination: Reads leaves it alone, and Names sets it. A transform that reads and sets nothing is generic over both, impl<K: ContextKind, Options>, and mounts anywhere. Transforms run in the order the chain writes them, then the app's publish layers, then the send. The chain is one type, built when the code compiles, so a transform costs only its own code. A reply of a batch handler takes batch transforms instead. A transform has no macro form: the same impl serves both forms, and only the mounting differs.

A reply transform carries the request's correlation id onto the reply. examples/publish_transform.rs /// Carries the request's correlation id onto its reply. `ForReply` reads the delivery being /// answered, so this transform mounts on a reply position. struct Correlate; impl<C, Options> PublishTransform<ForReply<C>, Options> for Correlate { type Destination = Reads; fn apply( &self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, cx: &PublishContext<'_, C>, ) { // The delivery's own buffer, shared rather than copied. if let Some(id) = cx.headers().get_shared("correlation-id") { out.headers_mut().insert("correlation-id", id); } } } A slot transform stamps a constant on what leaves the slot. examples/publish_transform.rs /// Stamps the schema version on what leaves a slot. `ForSlot` reads the slot's name and nothing /// else: the body that publishes has already read its delivery. struct SchemaVersion(&'static str); impl<Options> PublishTransform<ForSlot, Options> for SchemaVersion { type Destination = Reads; fn apply(&self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, _cx: &SlotContext<'_>) { out.headers_mut().insert("schema-version", self.0); } } Macros Manual examples/publish_transform.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // A transform follows the position it belongs to. b.include(confirm) .out_reply(Publish) .transform(Correlate) .include(audit) .out(Trail, Publish) .transform(SchemaVersion("2")) }) } examples/manual/publish_transform.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // A transform follows the position it belongs to. b.include(subscriber("orders", Confirm).reply().to("receipts").build()) .out_reply(Publish) .transform(Correlate) .include(subscriber("payments", AuditPayment).build()) .out(Trail, Publish) .transform(SchemaVersion("2")) }) }
A subscription over a replayable log opens at a position of your choice, and its handler can move it.

A handler moves its own subscription to another position of the log through the broker's seek handle. The in-memory broker's per-delivery context carries the handle under the key SeekHandle. A handler reads it with the Ctx<SeekHandle> parameter; the manual form declares MemoryContext on its Handle and reads ctx.context(SeekHandle). seek takes a MemoryPosition, the same type start_at takes. Once seek resolves, the next delivery comes from the new position, and entries already queued before it are skipped. A sequence the retention bound has already evicted is refused with an error, and the example retries the delivery then. The handle implements Seeker, the trait a broker with a replayable log provides. Ctx<SeekHandle> does not compile against MemoryBroker::new(), which keeps no log.

The handler meets a poison marker and moves its subscription past the entries behind it. Macros Manual examples/seek.rs /// The id that marks a poisoned region: the entries up to the resume point are skipped. const POISON: u64 = 999; #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "jobs")] struct Job { id: u64, } /// The seek handle is a field of the broker's per-delivery context, read with `Ctx`. #[subscriber("jobs", start_at(MemoryPosition::start()))] async fn work(job: &Job, Ctx(seeker): Ctx<SeekHandle>) -> HandlerOutcome { if job.id == POISON { // Resume at the fourth entry of the log. if seeker.seek(MemoryPosition::sequence(3)).await.is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } return HandlerOutcome::ack(); } tracing::info!(job.id, "processed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/seek.rs /// The id that marks a poisoned region: the entries up to the resume point are skipped. const POISON: u64 = 999; #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, schemars::JsonSchema)] struct Job { id: u64, } // `#[outgoing(name = "jobs")]` by hand: the type fixes its destination. impl OutgoingDestination for Job { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "jobs"; } impl MessageHeaders for Job { type Contract = NoHeaders; } struct Work; // Declaring the broker's `MemoryContext` is what puts the seek handle in the context. impl Handle<Job, (), (), MemoryContext> for Work { async fn handle( &self, job: &Job, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, MemoryContext>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { if job.id == POISON { // Resume at the fourth entry of the log. let seeker = ctx.context(SeekHandle); if seeker.seek(MemoryPosition::sequence(3)).await.is_err() { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } return Ok(()); } tracing::info!(job.id, "processed"); Ok(()) } } fn app(broker: MemoryBroker<Retaining>) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("jobs", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include( subscriber("jobs", Work) .start_at(MemoryPosition::start()) .build(), ) }) }

start_at opens a replayable subscription at a position: the start of the log, a sequence number, or the tip. A broker over a replayable log owns its position type; for the in-memory broker it is MemoryPosition. start_at(position) seeks the subscription before its first delivery, on every startup. It is one of the mount-site settings, and the attribute takes it as a clause too. Without it, the subscription opens at the broker's default; the in-memory broker's default is the tip of the log, so earlier entries are not delivered. MemoryPosition::start() is the oldest entry the broker still keeps, sequence(n) the n-th entry published to the name, counted from zero, and end() the tip. The in-memory broker keeps a log only when it is built with MemoryBroker::retaining. start_at does not compile against MemoryBroker::new(), which keeps nothing. A broker's subscription accepts a position when it implements Seekable.

The subscription opens at the start of the log and replays what was published before the service started. Macros Manual examples/seek.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "audit")] struct Entry { id: u64, } /// The audit trail opens at the start of the log, so it also reads what came before it. #[subscriber("audit", start_at(MemoryPosition::start()))] async fn record(entry: &Entry) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(entry.id, "recorded"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// Replaying reads what the broker kept, so this one keeps the last 64 entries of every name. /// `MemoryBroker::new()` keeps nothing, and a mount that seeks does not compile on it. fn broker() -> MemoryBroker<Retaining> { MemoryBroker::retaining(Retention::Messages(nonzero!(64))) } examples/manual/seek.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, schemars::JsonSchema)] struct Entry { id: u64, } // `#[outgoing(name = "audit")]` by hand: the type fixes its destination. impl OutgoingDestination for Entry { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "audit"; } impl MessageHeaders for Entry { type Contract = NoHeaders; } struct Record; impl Handle<Entry> for Record { fn handle( &self, entry: &Entry, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(entry.id, "recorded"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// Replaying reads what the broker kept, so this one keeps the last 64 entries of every name. /// `MemoryBroker::new()` keeps nothing, and a mount that seeks does not compile on it. fn broker() -> MemoryBroker<Retaining> { MemoryBroker::retaining(Retention::Messages(nonzero!(64))) } fn app(broker: MemoryBroker<Retaining>) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { // The audit trail opens at the start of the log, so it also reads what came before it. b.include( subscriber("audit", Record) .start_at(MemoryPosition::start()) .build(), ) }) }

max_attempts(n) ends a message that keeps coming back, and dead_letter(name) is where it goes then. max_attempts(n) counts the deliveries one message gets, the first one included. The delivery that reaches the cap is not retried: it is published to the dead_letter destination with its payload and headers. A cap without a destination rejects the delivery instead, and a warning names the subscription. The count is the broker's own where the transport keeps one, read through redelivery_count, and the framework's RETRY_COUNT_HEADER where it keeps none. The in-memory broker counts its deliveries, so the cap there counts its redeliveries. A retry() and a retry_after(delay) are both capped. Where the broker moves a spent delivery itself (a queue with a delivery limit and a dead-letter exchange), the declaration reaches the subscription descriptor at startup, and the broker applies it. The two steps come right after include, before .out_retry(..), the slot the dead-letter copy leaves through, and each is written once.

Macros Manual examples/retry.rs /// The gateway rejects this payment every time, so on its own it would never stop coming back. #[subscriber("payments")] async fn charge(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::warn!(payment.id, "gateway refused the charge"); HandlerOutcome::retry() } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // Three deliveries, then the payment goes to the dead-letter subject. b.include(charge) .max_attempts(nonzero!(3u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead") }) } examples/manual/retry.rs /// The gateway rejects this payment every time, so on its own it would never stop coming back. struct Charge; impl Handle<Payment> for Charge { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::warn!(payment.id, "gateway refused the charge"); ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // Three deliveries, then the payment goes to the dead-letter subject. b.include(subscriber("payments", Charge).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(3u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead") }) }

The Retry slot is the publisher a copy of a delivery leaves through; .out_retry(policy) replaces it and .to(name) names its destination. The runtime publishes a copy of a delivery in two cases: a delayed retry_after on a broker without native delayed redelivery, and a delivery sent to its dead_letter destination. Every registration has a publisher for those copies, paired from the broker's default publish policy. .out_retry(policy) replaces it; it is the Out slot Retry, so .codec(..) and .transform(..) follow it as on any slot. A copy carries the delivery's own bytes, so no codec encodes it, and its PublishTransforms read the delivery being retried. A copy sent back to the subscription carries the RETRY_COUNT_HEADER, incremented. On the in-memory broker the delay is native, so only the dead-letter copy leaves through this slot. A subscription whose source descriptor declares AddressedCopies reports where it is reached again, and copies go there. One that declares NamedCopies reads many destinations and addresses none: a wildcard, a filter, a pattern. On it the mount site names the destination with .to(name), or a transform names one per delivery. Without either, a router chain does not compile, and a mount in a broker scope refuses to start. A name given with .to(name) is a channel the registration sends to, and the generated document reports it. A broker that moves a spent delivery itself declares BrokerMoves, and .out_retry(..) does not compile there.

Macros Manual examples/settle_retry_destination.rs /// Stamps every copy with the subscription its delivery came from. struct RetriedFrom; impl<C, Options> PublishTransform<ForReply<C>, Options> for RetriedFrom { type Destination = Reads; fn apply( &self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, cx: &PublishContext<'_, C>, ) { out.headers_mut() .insert("x-retried-from", cx.name().to_owned()); } } #[subscriber("payments")] async fn charge(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::warn!(payment.id, "gateway refused the charge"); HandlerOutcome::retry() } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { b.include(charge) .max_attempts(nonzero!(2u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead") // Replaces the broker's default publisher for the copies of this registration. .out_retry(Publish) .transform(RetriedFrom) }) } examples/manual/settle_retry_destination.rs /// Stamps every copy with the subscription its delivery came from. struct RetriedFrom; impl<C, Options> PublishTransform<ForReply<C>, Options> for RetriedFrom { type Destination = Reads; fn apply( &self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, cx: &PublishContext<'_, C>, ) { out.headers_mut() .insert("x-retried-from", cx.name().to_owned()); } } struct Charge; impl Handle<Payment> for Charge { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::warn!(payment.id, "gateway refused the charge"); ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { b.include(subscriber("payments", Charge).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(2u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead") // Replaces the broker's default publisher for the copies of this registration. .out_retry(Publish) .transform(RetriedFrom) }) }

Macros Manual examples/settle_retry_destination.rs /// A subscription that reads every payment subject and addresses none of them, as a wildcard /// or a topic filter does. `Copies = NamedCopies` says so. #[derive(Debug, Clone)] struct PaymentFilter { pattern: &'static str, } impl PaymentFilter { const fn new(pattern: &'static str) -> Self { Self { pattern } } } impl SubscriptionSource<ConnectedMemoryBroker> for PaymentFilter { type Subscriber = MemorySubscriber<Discarding>; type Copies = NamedCopies; fn name(&self) -> &str { self.pattern } async fn subscribe( self, connected: &ConnectedMemoryBroker, ) -> Result<Self::Subscriber, MemoryError> { MemoryPattern::new(self.pattern).subscribe(connected).await } } #[subscriber(PaymentFilter::new("payments.*"))] async fn reconcile(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(payment.id, "not cleared yet"); HandlerOutcome::retry_after(Duration::from_secs(5)) } examples/manual/settle_retry_destination.rs /// A subscription that reads every payment subject and addresses none of them, as a wildcard /// or a topic filter does. `Copies = NamedCopies` says so. #[derive(Debug, Clone)] struct PaymentFilter { pattern: &'static str, } impl PaymentFilter { const fn new(pattern: &'static str) -> Self { Self { pattern } } } impl SubscriptionSource<ConnectedMemoryBroker> for PaymentFilter { type Subscriber = MemorySubscriber<Discarding>; type Copies = NamedCopies; fn name(&self) -> &str { self.pattern } async fn subscribe( self, connected: &ConnectedMemoryBroker, ) -> Result<Self::Subscriber, MemoryError> { MemoryPattern::new(self.pattern).subscribe(connected).await } } // What `subscriber(..)` accepts as a source: the descriptor passes through as it is. impl IntoSource for PaymentFilter { type Source = Self; fn into_source(self) -> Self { self } } struct Reconcile; impl Handle<Payment> for Reconcile { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(payment.id, "not cleared yet"); ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(Duration::from_secs(5)))) } } Macros Manual examples/settle_retry_destination.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // The descriptor addresses nothing, so the mount site names where a copy goes. b.include(reconcile).out_retry(Publish).to("payments.retry") }) } /// The same registration with no destination named. fn unnamed() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| b.include(reconcile)) } examples/manual/settle_retry_destination.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // The descriptor addresses nothing, so the mount site names where a copy goes. b.include(subscriber(PaymentFilter::new("payments.*"), Reconcile).build()) .out_retry(Publish) .to("payments.retry") }) } /// The same registration with no destination named. fn unnamed() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { b.include(subscriber(PaymentFilter::new("payments.*"), Reconcile).build()) }) }

A Router groups one module's handlers with their own middleware and codec, and include_router mounts the group on a broker. A router is a group of registrations bound to a broker type, not to a broker value, so a module builds it without a connection. include adds a #[subscriber] handler to the router the same way it adds one to a broker scope, settings included. A router's full type names every registration in a RouterDef, so a builder function returns impl RouterDef<B>, or Router<B, impl RouterDef<B>> when the caller still merges it. merge appends another router's registrations, and each router keeps its own codec and layers. include_router on a broker scope of the application mounts the group, as a step of the scope's chain before its includes. layer adds middleware and is called before the router's first include; after one, .layer(..) applies to that registration alone. A router's layer must be a BlanketLayer, because the router hides its handlers' types. The app's own layers wrap outside the router's layers. Router layers wrap single-message handlers; batch handlers are not wrapped. with_codec switches the codec mid-chain: registrations already added keep the codec they were added with. Without it, a router decodes with the default codec, JSON when the json feature is on.

Each module returns its router, and the service merges them and mounts the result. Macros Manual examples/routing.rs #[subscriber("orders")] async fn accept(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "accepted"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[subscriber("shipments")] async fn dispatch(shipment: &Shipment) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(shipment.order_id, "dispatched"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// The orders module's handlers. fn orders() -> Router<MemoryBroker, impl RouterDef<MemoryBroker>> { Router::new().include(accept) } /// The shipping module's handlers. fn shipping() -> Router<MemoryBroker, impl RouterDef<MemoryBroker>> { Router::new().include(dispatch) } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { b.include_router(orders().merge(shipping())) }) } examples/manual/routing.rs struct Accept; impl Handle<Order> for Accept { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "accepted"); ready(Ok(())) } } struct Dispatch; impl Handle<Shipment> for Dispatch { fn handle( &self, shipment: &Shipment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(shipment.order_id, "dispatched"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// The orders module's handlers. fn orders() -> Router<MemoryBroker, impl RouterDef<MemoryBroker>> { Router::new().include(subscriber("orders", Accept).build()) } /// The shipping module's handlers. fn shipping() -> Router<MemoryBroker, impl RouterDef<MemoryBroker>> { Router::new().include(subscriber("shipments", Dispatch).build()) } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { b.include_router(orders().merge(shipping())) }) }

Router::layer wraps every handler of the router, and nothing mounted outside it. Macros Manual examples/routing.rs /// Counts the deliveries of the handlers it wraps. #[derive(Clone)] struct Count(Arc<AtomicUsize>); struct Counted<H> { inner: H, count: Arc<AtomicUsize>, } // A router hides its handlers' types, so its layer wraps a handler of any type. impl BlanketLayer for Count { fn apply<M, C, S, H>(&self, handler: H) -> impl Handler<M, C, S> + 'static where M: Send + Sync + 'static, C: Send + 'static, S: Send + Sync + 'static, H: Handler<M, C, S> + 'static, { Counted { inner: handler, count: Arc::clone(&self.0), } } } impl<M, C, S, H> Handler<M, C, S> for Counted<H> where M: Send + Sync, C: Send, S: Send + Sync, H: Handler<M, C, S>, { async fn handle(&self, msg: &M, ctx: &mut Context<'_, C, S>) -> HandlerOutcome { self.count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed); self.inner.handle(msg, ctx).await } } #[subscriber("orders")] async fn accept(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "accepted"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[subscriber("shipments")] async fn dispatch(shipment: &Shipment) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(shipment.order_id, "dispatched"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn app(orders_seen: Arc<AtomicUsize>) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // The layer comes first and wraps every handler of this router. b.include_router(Router::new().layer(Count(orders_seen)).include(accept)) // Mounted on the scope, outside the router's layer. .include(dispatch) }) } examples/manual/routing.rs /// Counts the deliveries of the handlers it wraps. #[derive(Clone)] struct Count(Arc<AtomicUsize>); struct Counted<H> { inner: H, count: Arc<AtomicUsize>, } // A router hides its handlers' types, so its layer wraps a handler of any type. impl BlanketLayer for Count { fn apply<M, C, S, H>(&self, handler: H) -> impl Handler<M, C, S> + 'static where M: Send + Sync + 'static, C: Send + 'static, S: Send + Sync + 'static, H: Handler<M, C, S> + 'static, { Counted { inner: handler, count: Arc::clone(&self.0), } } } impl<M, C, S, H> Handler<M, C, S> for Counted<H> where M: Send + Sync, C: Send, S: Send + Sync, H: Handler<M, C, S>, { async fn handle(&self, msg: &M, ctx: &mut Context<'_, C, S>) -> HandlerOutcome { self.count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed); self.inner.handle(msg, ctx).await } } struct Accept; impl Handle<Order> for Accept { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "accepted"); ready(Ok(())) } } struct Dispatch; impl Handle<Shipment> for Dispatch { fn handle( &self, shipment: &Shipment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(shipment.order_id, "dispatched"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app(orders_seen: Arc<AtomicUsize>) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // The layer comes first and wraps every handler of this router. b.include_router( Router::new() .layer(Count(orders_seen)) .include(subscriber("orders", Accept).build()), ) // Mounted on the scope, outside the router's layer. .include(subscriber("shipments", Dispatch).build()) }) }

Router::with_codec sets the codec the registrations after it decode with. Macros Manual examples/routing.rs #[subscriber("orders")] async fn accept(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "accepted"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// The registrations after `with_codec` decode CBOR. fn orders() -> impl RouterDef<MemoryBroker> { Router::new().with_codec(CborCodec).include(accept) } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| b.include_router(orders())) } examples/manual/routing.rs struct Accept; impl Handle<Order> for Accept { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "accepted"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// The registrations after `with_codec` decode CBOR. fn orders() -> impl RouterDef<MemoryBroker> { Router::new() .with_codec(CborCodec) .include(subscriber("orders", Accept).build()) } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| b.include_router(orders())) }

A subscriber reads a subscription named by a string or by the broker's descriptor, fixed in the attribute or left to the mount site. The attribute fixes the kind of subscription and may leave its value to the mount site: Attribute Kind Value #[subscriber("orders")] by name fixed here #[subscriber] by name .name(..) at the mount site #[subscriber(MemorySource::new("orders"))] the broker's descriptor fixed here #[subscriber(MemorySource)] the broker's descriptor .name(..) at the mount site A name is a Name source and works on any broker that implements Subscribe, which opens its default subscription kind for that name. A descriptor is a type of the broker crate that implements SubscriptionSource and carries the broker's own settings, such as a consumer group or a durable name; the in-memory broker's is MemorySource. The macro reads the descriptor's type off the constructor call, so the expression ends in Type::new(..) and every step after it returns Self. A descriptor kind that the mount site names implements FromName. A source left open must be named: a mount without .name(..) does not compile. .name(..) is one of the mount-site settings and takes any string, so the name may come from configuration read before the app is built. A descriptor kind that needs more than a name, such as a Pulsar topic with its subscription, is written out in full in the attribute. In the manual form the first argument of subscriber is the source: a string, a descriptor, or Unnamed::<Kind>::new() for a source the mount site names, an Unnamed value.

The bare attribute leaves the name to the mount site. Macros Manual examples/subscriber_source.rs /// The attribute leaves the name open: the mount site gives it. #[subscriber] async fn audit(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "audited"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn app(shard: u32) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { b.include(audit.name(format!("audit-{shard}"))) }) } examples/manual/subscriber_source.rs struct Audit; impl Handle<Order> for Audit { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "audited"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app(shard: u32) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // `Unnamed<Name>` is no source yet: the mount does not compile until `.name(..)`. b.include( subscriber(Unnamed::<Name>::new(), Audit) .name(format!("audit-{shard}")) .build(), ) }) }

A descriptor is fixed in the attribute, or only its kind is, and the name comes at the mount site. Macros Manual examples/subscriber_source.rs /// The broker's descriptor, fixed in the attribute. #[subscriber(MemorySource::new("orders"))] async fn accept(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "accepted"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// The descriptor's kind in the attribute, its name at the mount site. #[subscriber(MemorySource)] async fn archive(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "archived"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { b.include(accept).include(archive.name("archive")) }) } examples/manual/subscriber_source.rs struct Accept; impl Handle<Order> for Accept { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "accepted"); ready(Ok(())) } } struct Archive; impl Handle<Order> for Archive { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "archived"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { // The broker's descriptor, built here. b.include(subscriber(MemorySource::new("orders"), Accept).build()) // The descriptor's kind, named at the mount site. .include( subscriber(Unnamed::<MemorySource>::new(), Archive) .name("archive") .build(), ) }) }

A serde struct is the header contract a handler reads and a publish writes, checked in both directions. A contract is a flat struct: each field names a header, and its value travels as a string. Fields are numbers, booleans, strings, bytes, unit-only enums, or Options of those. An Option field reads as None when its header is absent; any other missing field fails the contract. Header names are matched without regard to case; #[serde(rename = "..")] gives a wire name that is not a Rust identifier. Headers<T> parses the contract before the body runs. A contract that does not parse is a decode failure, settled by the subscriber's on_failure(decode = ..) policy. In a manual body Headers::<T>::from_context(ctx) parses it, and a failure there drops the delivery. The raw HeaderMap of a delivery stays on its context. What the handler publishes carries a contract of its own, declared on the outgoing type.

Macros Manual examples/typed_headers.rs /// What travels in the headers of a chunk: each field is one header, its value a string. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)] struct ChunkMeta { task_id: u64, chunk_no: u32, chunks_total: u32, } /// What travels in the headers of a finished chunk. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)] struct DoneMeta { task_id: u64, chunk_no: u32, } examples/manual/typed_headers.rs /// What travels in the headers of a chunk: each field is one header, its value a string. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)] struct ChunkMeta { task_id: u64, chunk_no: u32, chunks_total: u32, } /// What travels in the headers of a finished chunk. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)] struct DoneMeta { task_id: u64, chunk_no: u32, } Macros Manual examples/typed_headers.rs /// The contract is parsed before the body runs; what the body publishes carries its own. #[subscriber("chunks")] async fn convert( chunk: &Chunk, Headers(meta): Headers<ChunkMeta>, Out(events): Out<impl Publisher, Events>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(meta.task_id, meta.chunk_no, chunk.size, "converting"); let done = ChunkDone { output_key: format!("chunks/{}/{}.part", meta.task_id, meta.chunk_no), }; let done_meta = DoneMeta { task_id: meta.task_id, chunk_no: meta.chunk_no, }; match events .message(&done) .with_headers(&done_meta) .publish() .await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(_) => HandlerOutcome::retry(), } } examples/manual/typed_headers.rs /// The contract is parsed before the work starts; what the body publishes carries its own. struct Convert; impl<Entry> Handle<Chunk, (), Outs<(Entry,)>> for Convert where Entry: OutEntry<Events, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, chunk: &Chunk, outs: &Outs<(Entry,)>, ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let Headers(meta) = Headers::<ChunkMeta>::from_context(ctx).await?; tracing::info!(meta.task_id, meta.chunk_no, chunk.size, "converting"); let done = ChunkDone { output_key: format!("chunks/{}/{}.part", meta.task_id, meta.chunk_no), }; let done_meta = DoneMeta { task_id: meta.task_id, chunk_no: meta.chunk_no, }; let sent = outs .get(Events) .message(&done) .with_headers(&done_meta) .publish() .await; sent.map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } }

HeaderMap::insert_typed writes a header contract into a header map, the way a publish transform stamps every message of a slot. A field becomes one header named after it, its value written as a string. A None field writes nothing, and a header of the same name is overwritten. A field that holds a nested struct, a sequence or a map is an error. The example's transform is a publish transform on an Out slot, so every message the slot sends carries the contract.

Macros Manual examples/typed_headers.rs /// Where the service runs, as a contract stamped on everything the slot sends. #[derive(Clone, Serialize)] struct Origin { region: &'static str, canary: bool, } struct Stamp(Origin); impl<Options> PublishTransform<ForSlot, Options> for Stamp { type Destination = Reads; fn apply( &self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, _cx: &SlotContext<'_>, ) { if let Err(error) = out.headers_mut().insert_typed(&self.0) { tracing::warn!(%error, "origin headers left out"); } } } fn app() -> impl App { let origin = Origin { region: "eu-west", canary: false, }; RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("transcoder", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { b.include(convert) .out(Events, Publish) .transform(Stamp(origin)) }) } examples/manual/typed_headers.rs /// Where the service runs, as a contract stamped on everything the slot sends. #[derive(Clone, Serialize)] struct Origin { region: &'static str, canary: bool, } struct Stamp(Origin); impl<Options> PublishTransform<ForSlot, Options> for Stamp { type Destination = Reads; fn apply( &self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, _cx: &SlotContext<'_>, ) { if let Err(error) = out.headers_mut().insert_typed(&self.0) { tracing::warn!(%error, "origin headers left out"); } } } fn app() -> impl App { let origin = Origin { region: "eu-west", canary: false, }; RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("transcoder", "0.1.0")).with_broker(MemoryBroker::new(), |b| { b.include(subscriber("chunks", Convert).build()) .out(Events, Publish) .transform(Stamp(origin)) }) }

Message<H, T> hands a handler the decoded payload and its parsed header contract as one input. chunk.headers is the contract and chunk.body the payload. The contract parses the way Headers<T> parses it, and a contract that does not parse is a decode failure. A batch handler takes &[Message<H, T>], so each element keeps its own headers. A reply typed Message<H, T> carries its headers the same way.

Macros Manual examples/typed_headers.rs /// The payload and its contract arrive decoded together. #[subscriber("chunks")] async fn store(chunk: &Message<ChunkMeta, Chunk>) -> HandlerOutcome { let meta = &chunk.headers; if meta.chunk_no >= meta.chunks_total { // A chunk past the end of its task. return HandlerOutcome::drop(); } tracing::info!(meta.task_id, meta.chunk_no, chunk.body.size, "stored"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/typed_headers.rs /// The payload and its contract arrive decoded together. struct Store; impl Handle<Message<ChunkMeta, Chunk>> for Store { fn handle( &self, chunk: &Message<ChunkMeta, Chunk>, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { let meta = &chunk.headers; if meta.chunk_no >= meta.chunks_total { // A chunk past the end of its task. return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::drop())); } tracing::info!(meta.task_id, meta.chunk_no, chunk.body.size, "stored"); ready(Ok(())) } }

A message type names its header contract, so publishing it does not compile without the headers. #[outgoing(headers = Meta)] makes the contract part of the message type, the type's MessageHeaders contract. Its publish does not compile without .with_headers(&meta). The manual form implements MessageHeaders by hand and names the contract as its Contract; a type with none names NoHeaders. An Out slot lists the types it may publish in #[publishes(..)], and each keeps its own contract, as on the Slots page. The handler on the Headers page publishes a ChunkDone through such a slot.

Macros Manual examples/typed_headers.rs /// A chunk: publishing one does not compile without its `ChunkMeta`. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "chunks", headers = ChunkMeta)] struct Chunk { size: u64, } /// A finished chunk: publishing one does not compile without its `DoneMeta`. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "chunks.done", headers = DoneMeta)] struct ChunkDone { output_key: String, } examples/manual/typed_headers.rs /// A chunk: publishing one does not compile without its `ChunkMeta`. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)] struct Chunk { size: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Chunk { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "chunks"; } impl MessageHeaders for Chunk { type Contract = WithHeaders<ChunkMeta>; } /// A finished chunk: publishing one does not compile without its `DoneMeta`. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)] struct ChunkDone { output_key: String, } impl OutgoingDestination for ChunkDone { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "chunks.done"; } impl MessageHeaders for ChunkDone { type Contract = WithHeaders<DoneMeta>; } Macros Manual examples/typed_headers.rs /// The slot the converter publishes through, and what it may publish. #[derive(OutSlot)] #[publishes(ChunkDone)] struct Events; examples/manual/typed_headers.rs /// The slot the converter publishes through, and what it may publish. struct Events; impl OutSlot for Events { const NAME: &'static str = "Events"; type Destination = Reads; fn outgoing() -> Vec<OutgoingMessageMetadata> { <ChunkDone as OutMessages<Self>>::outgoing() } } impl PublishedThrough<Events> for ChunkDone {} impl<M: OutSlot> OutMessages<M> for ChunkDone { fn outgoing() -> Vec<OutgoingMessageMetadata> { vec![OutgoingMessageMetadata::new( Self::DESTINATION, type_name::<Self>(), )] } }

Руководства ведут от пустого крейта к работающему сервису на RustStream. Установка: крейт, его фичи cargo и крейт брокера. Быстрый старт: работающий сервис из шаблона cargo generate. Учебник: сервис заказов с типом сообщения, обработчиком, ответом и роутером на брокере в памяти. Навыки для агентов: навыки, с которыми ИИ-агент пишет сервисы, тесты и крейты брокеров рекомендованным путём. Строим сервис шаг за шагом: магазин, который строится глава за главой: от первого подписчика до сетевого брокера. Брокеры: крейты брокеров и перевод сервиса на другой брокер.

Одиннадцать глав строят один сервис на RustStream, небольшой магазин: от первого подписчика до сетевого брокера. Магазин принимает заказ, списывает оплату, отправляет заказ и уведомляет покупателя. Каждый шаг - это подписчик, и шаги обмениваются сообщениями через темы. Магазин работает на in-memory брокере, поэтому для любой главы ничего не нужно устанавливать. Каждая глава подключает нужные ей компоненты и ссылается на их страницы в разделе Компоненты. У каждого блока кода две вкладки: «Макросы» с атрибутами и derive-макросами и «Вручную» с тем же кодом, написанным без них. Готовый магазин лежит в репозитории в examples/guide, а его ручная версия - в examples/manual/guide. CI собирает обе версии и запускает их тесты при каждом изменении. Каждая часть магазина - отдельный модуль: orders.rs, payments.rs, shipping.rs и notifications.rs. state.rs содержит то, что подписчики используют совместно, observability.rs - собственный middleware магазина, а service.rs собирает приложение. main.rs - точка входа командной строки, а http.rs запускает тот же магазин рядом с HTTP-сервером.

asyncapi gen печатает AsyncAPI-документ магазина: все темы, кто их читает и пишет, схемы, ограничение попыток и описание, которое приложение даёт себе. Документ строится по самому приложению, поэтому он не может описать тему, которую код не использует. Каждая подписка - это операция receive, каждый ответ и каждый слот - операция send. Схема полезной нагрузки берётся из её derive-макроса JsonSchema, а doc-комментарий становится описанием. max_attempts и dead_letter указываются на операции, поэтому читатель видит, куда попадает сообщение, обработка которого не удаётся. Раздел AsyncAPI описывает серверы, схемы безопасности и раздачу документа по HTTP. Для документа нужна фича asyncapi крейта.

main.rs собирает магазин на in-memory брокере. #[ruststream::app] даёт исполняемому файлу команды: run запускает магазин, asyncapi gen печатает документ. Макросы Вручную main.rs /// `run` starts the shop; `asyncapi gen` prints its AsyncAPI document. #[ruststream::app(flavor = "current_thread")] fn app() -> impl App<State = Shop> { service::shop(MemoryBroker::new()) } main.rs fn app() -> impl App<State = Shop> { service::shop(MemoryBroker::new()) } /// What `#[ruststream::app]` writes: `run` starts the shop; `asyncapi gen` prints its AsyncAPI /// document. fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main_on(AppRuntime::CurrentThread, app) }

AppInfo - это блок info документа: название, версия, описание, контакт, лицензия и теги. Макросы Вручную service.rs /// What the AsyncAPI document says about the shop. fn info() -> AppInfo { AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0") .description("Takes orders, charges them, ships them and tells the customer.") .contact(Contact::new().name("Shop team").email("shop@example.com")) .license(License::new("Apache-2.0")) .tag(Tag::new("orders")) } service.rs /// What the AsyncAPI document says about the shop. fn info() -> AppInfo { AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0") .description("Takes orders, charges them, ships them and tells the customer.") .contact(Contact::new().name("Shop team").email("shop@example.com")) .license(License::new("Apache-2.0")) .tag(Tag::new("orders")) }

cargo run --example guide --features testing,macros,memory,json,cbor,asyncapi -- asyncapi gen --yaml Операция подписчика charge читает тему, отвечает в payments.settled и объявляет ограничение попыток: receive_payments_requested: action: receive channel: $ref: '#/channels/payments.requested' messages: - $ref: '#/channels/payments.requested/messages/PaymentRequest' description: Charges an order through the payment provider. reply: channel: $ref: '#/channels/payments.settled' messages: - $ref: '#/channels/payments.settled/messages/Paid' x-ruststream-retry: maxAttempts: 5 deadLetter: payments.dead Обе формы магазина выдают одинаковый документ. Тест в каждой из них сравнивает документ с examples/guide/asyncapi.json, поэтому любое изменение темы видно на ревью.

Упаковка - это вычисления, поэтому ей выделены два собственных потока. Бронирование курьера ждёт сети, поэтому четыре бронирования идут одновременно. По умолчанию подписка обрабатывает доставки по одной, в том порядке, в каком их передаёт брокер. Воркеры позволяют ей обрабатывать несколько доставок одновременно на рантайме приложения. Они подходят для обработчика, который ждёт ввода-вывода. Потоки выделяют подписке собственные потоки. Они подходят для обработчика, который ведёт вычисления: иначе он задерживал бы рантайм, который обслуживает все остальные подписки. И воркеры, и потоки - настройки подписки, тело обработчика при этом не меняется. Подписка с воркерами или потоками больше не сохраняет порядок доставок. workers(n, by_key) сохраняет порядок для каждого ключа.

pack разбивает оплаченный заказ на посылки и отвечает планом упаковки. Оплаченный заказ за границами магазина отбрасывается до того, как спланирована хоть одна посылка. threads(2) запускает вместе с подпиской два потока, и доставки распределяются между ними по очереди. Декодирование, тело обработчика, ответ и завершение доставки выполняются в потоке, который получил доставку. Макросы Вручную shipping.rs /// Packs a paid order into parcels. // Packing is computation: two threads of its own keep it off the app's runtime, which serves I/O. #[subscriber("payments.settled", threads(2), reply)] async fn pack(paid: &Paid) -> Result<Packed, HandlerOutcome> { if !within_bounds(&paid.lines) { tracing::warn!( order = paid.order, "a paid order past the shop's bounds, dropped" ); return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); } Ok(Packed { order: paid.order, customer: paid.customer.clone(), parcels: plan(&paid.lines), }) } shipping.rs /// Packs a paid order into parcels. struct Pack; impl Handle<Paid, Packed, (), (), Shop> for Pack { fn handle( &self, paid: &Paid, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_, (), Shop>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Packed, HandlerOutcome>> { if !within_bounds(&paid.lines) { tracing::warn!( order = paid.order, "a paid order past the shop's bounds, dropped" ); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::drop())); } ready(Ok(Packed { order: paid.order, customer: paid.customer.clone(), parcels: plan(&paid.lines), })) } }

dispatch бронирует курьера для упакованного заказа и сообщает покупателю код отслеживания. workers(4) допускает до четырёх бронирований одновременно. Следующая доставка ждёт свободного воркера. Макросы Вручную shipping.rs /// Books a courier for a packed order and tells the customer. // Booking waits on the courier's API, so four bookings run at once. #[subscriber("shipping.packed", workers(4))] async fn dispatch(packed: &Packed, Out(notices): Out<impl Publisher, Notices>) -> HandlerOutcome { let tracking = book_courier(packed).await; let notice = Notice { customer: packed.customer.clone(), text: format!("Order {} is on its way: {tracking}.", packed.order), }; match notices.message(&notice).publish().await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(_) => HandlerOutcome::retry(), } } shipping.rs /// Books a courier for a packed order and tells the customer. struct Dispatch; impl<Entry> Handle<Packed, (), Outs<(Entry,)>, (), Shop> for Dispatch where Entry: OutEntry<Notices, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, packed: &Packed, outs: &Outs<(Entry,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_, (), Shop>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let tracking = book_courier(packed).await; let notice = Notice { customer: packed.customer.clone(), text: format!("Order {} is on its way: {tracking}.", packed.order), }; let sent = outs.get(Notices).message(&notice).publish().await; sent.map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } }

Роутер отгрузки читает внутренние темы магазина, поэтому декодирует CBOR. Ответ использует кодек по умолчанию, если его позиция не задаёт другой, поэтому ответ pack задаёт CBOR. Слот использует кодек роутера, если не задаёт свой, поэтому уведомления задают JSON. В ручной форме обе настройки - шаги цепочки монтирования: threads и workers. Счётная часть работает на своих потоках, поэтому рантайм приложения только ждёт ввода-вывода, и магазин запускает его в потоке, который вызывает main: #[ruststream::app(flavor = "current_thread")], а в ручной форме run_main_on(AppRuntime::CurrentThread, app). Точка входа с HTTP из главы про HTTP делает то же через #[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")]. Макросы Вручную shipping.rs /// The shipping side's subscribers. Both read the shop's own topics, so both decode CBOR. pub(crate) fn routes() -> impl RouterDef<MemoryBroker, Shop> { Router::new() .with_codec(INTERNAL) .include(pack) // A reply encodes with the default codec unless its position names one. .out_reply(Publish) .codec(INTERNAL) .build() .include(dispatch) // A slot encodes with the router's codec unless it names one; notices stay JSON. .out(Notices, Publish) .codec(JsonCodec) .build() } shipping.rs /// The shipping side's subscribers. Both read the shop's own topics, so both decode CBOR. pub(crate) fn routes() -> impl RouterDef<MemoryBroker, Shop> { Router::new() .with_codec(INTERNAL) .include( subscriber(Paid::DESTINATION, Pack) .describe("Packs a paid order into parcels.") // Packing is computation: two threads of its own keep it off the app's runtime. .threads(nonzero!(2)) .reply() .build(), ) // A reply encodes with the default codec unless its position names one. .out_reply(Publish) .codec(INTERNAL) .build() .include( subscriber(Packed::DESTINATION, Dispatch) .describe("Books a courier for a packed order and tells the customer.") // Booking waits on the courier's API, so four bookings run at once. .workers(nonzero!(4)) .build(), ) // A slot encodes with the router's codec unless it names one; notices stay JSON. .out(Notices, Publish) .codec(JsonCodec) .build() } Потоки окупаются, когда вычисления занимают от десяти микросекунд на доставку. На более лёгком обработчике они обходятся дороже, чем экономят. Диагностика опроса находит обработчики, которые задерживают рантайм.

Витрина принимает заказы по HTTP и сохраняет их вместе с событиями. Ретранслятор передаёт события брокеру, а магазин работает рядом с сервером. Когда сервис также обслуживает HTTP, процессом управляет HTTP-сервер, а магазин работает рядом с ним. start запускает магазин в фоне и возвращает управление, когда магазин работает. Поэтому если брокер отказывает в подключении, процесс останавливается раньше, чем сервер примет первый запрос. HTTP-запрос не должен сам публиковать сообщения в брокер. Иначе сбой брокера приведёт к ошибке запроса, а заказ, сохранённый без события, никогда не дойдёт до магазина. Транзакционный outbox решает обе проблемы. Запрос записывает заказ и его событие в одной транзакции, а ретранслятор позже публикует сохранённые события. Сбой брокера только откладывает события, и ни одно из них не теряется. Если процесс аварийно завершится между публикацией и удалением события, событие будет опубликовано снова, поэтому магазин получает каждый заказ хотя бы один раз.

В настоящей базе данных заказы и outbox - это две таблицы, которые записываются в одной транзакции. Здесь эту роль играет мьютекс над парой. Пережить сбой события могут только в настоящей базе данных: здесь строки хранятся в памяти, и при сбое неопубликованные пропадают. Макросы Вручную http.rs /// The orders the storefront took, and the events the shop still owes the broker. With a real /// database both writes run in one transaction; the mutex over the pair plays that role here. #[derive(Default)] struct Store { orders: Vec<Order>, outbox: VecDeque<(RequestMeta, Order)>, } http.rs /// The orders the storefront took, and the events the shop still owes the broker. With a real /// database both writes run in one transaction; the mutex over the pair plays that role here. #[derive(Default)] struct Store { orders: Vec<Order>, outbox: VecDeque<(RequestMeta, Order)>, } HTTP-часть и outbox - обычные функции, поэтому обе вкладки показывают один и тот же код.

POST /orders принимает заказ в JSON, а идентификатор запроса - из заголовка x-request-id. Она только записывает в хранилище, поэтому отвечает 202 Accepted, не дожидаясь брокера. На заказ за границами магазина она отвечает 400 Bad Request и не сохраняет его. Макросы Вручную http.rs /// Takes an order over HTTP. The request only writes to the store, so no broker I/O can fail or /// stall the response. async fn place_order( State(store): State<Arc<Mutex<Store>>>, headers: HeaderMap, Json(order): Json<Order>, ) -> (StatusCode, &'static str) { let request_id = headers .get("x-request-id") .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()) .unwrap_or("unknown") .to_owned(); if total_cents(&order.lines).is_none() { return ( StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "the order is past the shop's bounds
", ); } { let mut store = store.lock().await; store.orders.push(order.clone()); store.outbox.push_back((RequestMeta { request_id }, order)); } (StatusCode::ACCEPTED, "accepted
") } http.rs /// Takes an order over HTTP. The request only writes to the store, so no broker I/O can fail or /// stall the response. async fn place_order( State(store): State<Arc<Mutex<Store>>>, headers: HeaderMap, Json(order): Json<Order>, ) -> (StatusCode, &'static str) { let request_id = headers .get("x-request-id") .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()) .unwrap_or("unknown") .to_owned(); if total_cents(&order.lines).is_none() { return ( StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "the order is past the shop's bounds
", ); } { let mut store = store.lock().await; store.orders.push(order.clone()); store.outbox.push_back((RequestMeta { request_id }, order)); } (StatusCode::ACCEPTED, "accepted
") }

Ретранслятор публикует сначала самое старое событие вместе с его контрактом заголовков и удаляет событие только после успешной публикации. Если публикация вернула ошибку, строка остаётся до следующего прохода. Ретранслятор работает, пока процесс его не остановит, а затем делает последний проход. Издатель - любой Publisher, поэтому ретранслятор не меняется при смене брокера. Макросы Вручную http.rs /// Hands the outbox to the broker, oldest event first. A row leaves the outbox only after its /// publish succeeded, so a broker outage delays events and loses none. async fn relay_pending(store: &Mutex<Store>, egress: &impl Publisher) { loop { let Some((meta, order)) = store.lock().await.outbox.front().cloned() else { return; }; let sent = egress .message(&order) .with_headers(&meta) .with_codec(JsonCodec) .publish() .await; if sent.is_err() { // The row stays for the next round. return; } store.lock().await.outbox.pop_front(); } } /// Runs the relay every 200 milliseconds until `stop` completes, then runs it once more. async fn relay_outbox( store: Arc<Mutex<Store>>, egress: impl Publisher, stop: impl Future<Output = ()>, ) { let mut rounds = time::interval(Duration::from_millis(200)); tokio::pin!(stop); loop { tokio::select! { biased; () = &mut stop => break, _ = rounds.tick() => relay_pending(&store, &egress).await, } } // The last round runs once no request writes a row any more, so it empties the outbox. relay_pending(&store, &egress).await; } http.rs /// Hands the outbox to the broker, oldest event first. A row leaves the outbox only after its /// publish succeeded, so a broker outage delays events and loses none. async fn relay_pending(store: &Mutex<Store>, egress: &impl Publisher) { loop { let Some((meta, order)) = store.lock().await.outbox.front().cloned() else { return; }; let sent = egress .message(&order) .with_headers(&meta) .with_codec(JsonCodec) .publish() .await; if sent.is_err() { // The row stays for the next round. return; } store.lock().await.outbox.pop_front(); } } /// Runs the relay every 200 milliseconds until `stop` completes, then runs it once more. async fn relay_outbox( store: Arc<Mutex<Store>>, egress: impl Publisher, stop: impl Future<Output = ()>, ) { let mut rounds = time::interval(Duration::from_millis(200)); tokio::pin!(stop); loop { tokio::select! { biased; () = &mut stop => break, _ = rounds.tick() => relay_pending(&store, &egress).await, } } // The last round runs once no request writes a row any more, so it empties the outbox. relay_pending(&store, &egress).await; }

bindable позволяет процессу получить токен издателя до запуска магазина, а publisher превращает токен в работающего издателя после подключения брокера. Сервер останавливается по Ctrl+C или когда stopping сообщает, что магазин остановился сам. Когда HTTP-сервер завершил запросы, процесс останавливает ретранслятор, и его последний проход передаёт брокеру оставшиеся строки, пока магазин ещё работает. Затем магазин дорабатывает начатые доставки и останавливается через shutdown. MemoryBroker тоже хранит очереди в памяти процесса: заказ, который последний проход передал, а магазин не успел забрать до остановки, пропадёт вместе с процессом. Брокер, который хранит сообщения, сбережёт его до следующего запуска. main, написанный вручную, сам устанавливает логгер через ruststream::logging::init(). Макросы Вручную http.rs #[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")] async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { logging::init()?; let broker = MemoryBroker::new().bindable(); // A token now, a live publisher once the shop has connected the broker. let egress = broker.bind(Publish); // The shop starts first: a broker that refuses to connect stops the process before HTTP // takes a request. let running = shop(broker).start().await?; let egress = running.publisher(egress).await?; let store = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Store::default())); let stop_relay = CancellationToken::new(); let relay = tokio::spawn(relay_outbox( Arc::clone(&store), egress, stop_relay.clone().cancelled_owned(), )); let router = axum::Router::new() .route("/orders", post(place_order)) .with_state(store); let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:8080").await?; tracing::info!("storefront on http://127.0.0.1:8080/orders"); // HTTP stops on Ctrl+C, or when the shop stops on its own; the shop then drains. let stopping = running.stopping(); axum::serve(listener, router) .with_graceful_shutdown(async move { tokio::select! { _ = signal::ctrl_c() => {} () = stopping => {} } }) .await?; // HTTP has drained, so no request writes a row any more: the relay's last round hands the // pending rows over while the shop still runs, and only then does the shop drain. stop_relay.cancel(); relay.await?; running.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) } http.rs #[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")] async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { logging::init()?; let broker = MemoryBroker::new().bindable(); // A token now, a live publisher once the shop has connected the broker. let egress = broker.bind(Publish); // The shop starts first: a broker that refuses to connect stops the process before HTTP // takes a request. let running = shop(broker).start().await?; let egress = running.publisher(egress).await?; let store = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Store::default())); let stop_relay = CancellationToken::new(); let relay = tokio::spawn(relay_outbox( Arc::clone(&store), egress, stop_relay.clone().cancelled_owned(), )); let router = axum::Router::new() .route("/orders", post(place_order)) .with_state(store); let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:8080").await?; tracing::info!("storefront on http://127.0.0.1:8080/orders"); // HTTP stops on Ctrl+C, or when the shop stops on its own; the shop then drains. let stopping = running.stopping(); axum::serve(listener, router) .with_graceful_shutdown(async move { tokio::select! { _ = signal::ctrl_c() => {} () = stopping => {} } }) .await?; // HTTP has drained, so no request writes a row any more: the relay's last round hands the // pending rows over while the shop still runs, and only then does the shop drain. stop_relay.cancel(); relay.await?; running.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) } Запустите магазин и оформите заказ: cargo run --example guide_http --features testing,macros,memory,json,cbor,asyncapi,logging curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/orders -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -H 'x-request-id: req-1' \ -d '{"id":1,"customer":"ada@example.com","lines":[{"sku":"mug","quantity":12,"price_cents":1200}]}' Журнал из главы 5 показывает путь заказа через магазин. Конечная точка проверки состояния того же сервера сообщает оркестратору о состоянии магазина.

Заказ получает строки, контракт заголовков, обязательный при каждой публикации, и кодек, выбранный для каждой темы. Полезная нагрузка - это любой тип serde. Кодек превращает её в байты и обратно. Заголовки передаются рядом с полезной нагрузкой. Контракт заголовков - это структура serde, в которой каждое поле соответствует одному заголовку. Тип сообщения, объявивший контракт, нельзя опубликовать без заголовков: такая публикация не компилируется. Подписчик читает контракт через параметр Headers<T>, который разбирается до запуска тела обработчика. Доставка с заголовками, которые не удалось разобрать, не доходит до тела и отбрасывается, как и полезная нагрузка, которую не удалось декодировать. Кодек задаётся в точке монтирования, а не на типе. Поэтому один тип может передаваться в одной теме в JSON, а в другой - в CBOR.

Дальше код магазина разложен по модулям. orders.rs содержит заказ: его строки, итоговую сумму и контракт заголовков, с которым он публикуется. Границы ограничивают, сколько может запросить один заказ, а сумма считается с проверкой переполнения, поэтому у заказа за этими границами суммы нет. Макросы Вручную orders.rs /// How many lines an order may hold. pub(crate) const MAX_LINES: usize = 100; /// How many items one line may order. pub(crate) const MAX_QUANTITY: u32 = 1_000; /// The highest price of one item, in cents. pub(crate) const MAX_PRICE_CENTS: u64 = 1_000_000; /// One line of an order: what the customer buys, how many, and at what price. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] pub(crate) struct Line { pub(crate) sku: String, pub(crate) quantity: u32, pub(crate) price_cents: u64, } /// An order placed in the storefront. It travels with the headers of the request that placed it. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "orders.placed", headers = RequestMeta)] pub(crate) struct Order { pub(crate) id: u64, pub(crate) customer: String, pub(crate) lines: Vec<Line>, } /// Whether `lines` stay within the shop's bounds. pub(crate) fn within_bounds(lines: &[Line]) -> bool { lines.len() <= MAX_LINES && lines .iter() .all(|line| line.quantity <= MAX_QUANTITY && line.price_cents <= MAX_PRICE_CENTS) } /// What `lines` cost together, or `None` past the shop's bounds. pub(crate) fn total_cents(lines: &[Line]) -> Option<u64> { if !within_bounds(lines) { return None; } lines.iter().try_fold(0_u64, |total, line| { total.checked_add(u64::from(line.quantity).checked_mul(line.price_cents)?) }) } orders.rs /// How many lines an order may hold. pub(crate) const MAX_LINES: usize = 100; /// How many items one line may order. pub(crate) const MAX_QUANTITY: u32 = 1_000; /// The highest price of one item, in cents. pub(crate) const MAX_PRICE_CENTS: u64 = 1_000_000; /// One line of an order: what the customer buys, how many, and at what price. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] pub(crate) struct Line { pub(crate) sku: String, pub(crate) quantity: u32, pub(crate) price_cents: u64, } /// An order placed in the storefront. It travels with the headers of the request that placed it. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] pub(crate) struct Order { pub(crate) id: u64, pub(crate) customer: String, pub(crate) lines: Vec<Line>, } // What `#[derive(Outgoing)]` with `#[outgoing(name = "orders.placed", headers = RequestMeta)]` // writes: the destination, the headers a publish must carry, and the name in the document. impl OutgoingDestination for Order { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "orders.placed"; } impl MessageHeaders for Order { type Contract = WithHeaders<RequestMeta>; } impl MessageInfo for Order { const NAME: &'static str = "Order"; const DESCRIPTION: Option<&'static str> = Some( "An order placed in the storefront. It travels with the headers of the request that \ placed it.", ); } /// Whether `lines` stay within the shop's bounds. pub(crate) fn within_bounds(lines: &[Line]) -> bool { lines.len() <= MAX_LINES && lines .iter() .all(|line| line.quantity <= MAX_QUANTITY && line.price_cents <= MAX_PRICE_CENTS) } /// What `lines` cost together, or `None` past the shop's bounds. pub(crate) fn total_cents(lines: &[Line]) -> Option<u64> { if !within_bounds(lines) { return None; } lines.iter().try_fold(0_u64, |total, line| { total.checked_add(u64::from(line.quantity).checked_mul(line.price_cents)?) }) } headers = RequestMeta делает контракт частью типа. Ручная форма выражает то же через type Contract = WithHeaders<RequestMeta> и задаёт имя сообщения в AsyncAPI-документе реализацией MessageInfo.

Каждое поле контракта - один заголовок. request_id указывает запрос к витрине, который оформил заказ, чтобы каждый шаг мог записать его в журнал. Макросы Вручную orders.rs /// The headers of a placed order: each field is one header. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] pub(crate) struct RequestMeta { pub(crate) request_id: String, } orders.rs /// The headers of a placed order: each field is one header. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] pub(crate) struct RequestMeta { pub(crate) request_id: String, }

audit - второй подписчик темы orders.placed. Он записывает каждый заказ в журнал аудита вместе с запросом, который его оформил. Каждая подписка получает все сообщения своей темы, поэтому каждый заказ видят и audit, и accept из следующей главы. Ручная форма принимает на вход пару Message<RequestMeta, Order>: обе части декодируются до запуска тела, а AsyncAPI-документ показывает схему заголовков. Макросы Вручную orders.rs /// Writes every placed order to the audit log, with the request that placed it. #[subscriber("orders.placed")] async fn audit(order: &Order, Headers(meta): Headers<RequestMeta>) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!( request = %meta.request_id, order = order.id, total_cents = total_cents(&order.lines), "order placed", ); HandlerOutcome::ack() } orders.rs /// Writes every placed order to the audit log, with the request that placed it. struct Audit; // The input is the pair of headers and payload: both decode before the body runs, and the // document shows the header schema, as a `Headers<RequestMeta>` parameter does with the macros. impl Handle<Message<RequestMeta, Order>, (), (), (), Shop> for Audit { fn handle( &self, placed: &Message<RequestMeta, Order>, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_, (), Shop>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { let (meta, order) = (&placed.headers, &placed.body); tracing::info!( request = %meta.request_id, order = order.id, total_cents = total_cents(&order.lines), "order placed", ); ready(Ok(())) } }

JSON - кодек по умолчанию. Магазин оставляет его для тем orders.placed и notices, которые читают другие команды. Темы между шагами самого магазина передают сообщения в CBOR: этот формат компактнее, а других читателей у этих тем нет. Кодек задаётся одной константой, поэтому роутеры следующих глав не могут разойтись в выборе. Макросы Вручную payments.rs /// The codec of the topics between the shop's own steps: CBOR is smaller than JSON, and no /// other team reads them. pub(crate) const INTERNAL: CborCodec = CborCodec; payments.rs /// The codec of the topics between the shop's own steps: CBOR is smaller than JSON, and no /// other team reads them. pub(crate) const INTERNAL: CborCodec = CborCodec; Роутер декодирует сообщения кодеком, который задаёт with_codec, а каждая позиция публикации задаёт свой кодек через .codec(..). Следующая глава использует обе возможности. Для CBOR нужна фича cbor крейта.

Приложение оборачивает каждого подписчика в два слоя: один пишет в журнал доставки и их исходы, другой, собственный, предупреждает о медленных обработчиках. Layer оборачивает обработчик в другой обработчик. Слой выполняет код до тела обработчика, после него или вместо него и передаёт исход дальше. Слой приложения оборачивает всех подписчиков, которых монтирует приложение. Слой роутера оборачивает только подписчиков этого роутера. RustStream сам записывает события через tracing: запуск сервиса, подписку на каждую тему, остановку сервиса. TracingLayer добавляет событие для каждой доставки: delivery received на уровне DEBUG, затем её исход. Подтверждение (ack) записывается на уровне INFO, переобработка и отбрасывание - на уровне WARN. Фича logging выводит эти события, как показала глава 1. Вместо неё подходит любой другой подписчик tracing. Раздел Наблюдаемость описывает метрики Prometheus и экспорт в OpenTelemetry. Они подключаются как слои тем же способом.

SlowHandlers замеряет время каждого обработчика и предупреждает, если обработчик работает дольше порога. Предупреждение называет подписку, имя которой слой читает из контекста доставки.
